localPatchStatus: Local pinned 8.19.0 backport; the upstream proposal is open, not merged or blindly installed. Deterministic processed-source naming preserves precision and explicit defines; additional feedback identity, per-context reflection, shader-layout isolation and private back-buffer cleanup are locally tested. Native rendering and heap acceptance remain unverified.
purpose: Deterministic processed GL identities; context-owned reflection and deletion; pooled mask source detachment; render-target source listener cleanup. Local backport, not upstream PR installation.
maskLifecyclePatch: Local AlphaMaskEffect reset clears its completed mask source before pool reuse. This separate lifecycle fix does not claim upstream proposal coverage.
renderTargetLifecyclePatch: Local RenderTargetSystem cleanup removes only its own source destroy callbacks. Source destruction retains target cleanup and removes the callback registry entry. This separate fix does not claim upstream proposal coverage or native heap acceptance.
graphicsBatchReusePatch: Local GraphicsContextSystem bind-group preparation visits only the current batch count, not stale array tails retained by pooled render data. This separate lifecycle fix does not claim upstream proposal coverage or native remount acceptance.

managedResourceLifecyclePatch: Local GCManagedHash removal detaches only its own unload callback, including already-absent GPU data. Shared buffers retain other renderer and user callbacks. This separate lifecycle fix does not claim complete heap stability.
batchBindGroupLifecyclePatch: Local texture batch bind-group cache evicts its own entry on group destruction, while preserving live reuse and other groups. Destroyed resource/key shells no longer accumulate in the module cache. This does not claim whole-heap stability.
rendererCachePatch: Renderer IDs remain unique numbers but use negative keys so per-renderer object caches do not grow sparse indexed backing arrays. Released managed GPU data keys are deleted after teardown.
textureBatchIdPatch: TextureSource IDs remain unique numbers but use negative keys, so per-batch numeric lookups do not allocate sparse indexed storage. BatchTextureArray.clear deletes released ID entries.
